title: Why Do We Have Music? Let's Find Out!

mason.name: Mason
mason.persona: cheerful 9-year-old boy, curious and full of questions

irene.name: Irene
irene.persona: friendly 11-year-old girl, confident, loves playing instruments

focusWords.kidDefinition: A thing you play to make music.
examples: Irene can play three musical instruments.
Mason wants to learn a new instrument this year.
focusWords.greekHint: Μουσικό όργανο: ένα εργαλείο για να βγάλεις μουσική.

focusWords.kidDefinition: An instrument with strings that you play with a bow or your fingers.
examples: The harp is a string instrument with many strings.
Irene practises the violin, which is a string instrument.
focusWords.greekHint: Έγχορδο: έχει χορδές, όπως η κιθάρα.

focusWords.kidDefinition: An instrument you play by blowing air into it.
examples: The trumpet is a wind instrument that is very loud.
Mason blows gently into his recorder, a wind instrument.

focusWords.kidDefinition: An instrument you hit, shake, or tap to make a sound.
examples: The drum is a percussion instrument that makes a big sound.
Mason shakes a tambourine, another percussion instrument, to keep the beat.
focusWords.greekHint: Κρουστό: το χτυπάς ή το κουνάς.

focusWords.kidDefinition: The sound you make when you speak or sing.
examples: Irene has a warm, friendly voice when she sings.
Mason uses his voice to count the beats in the song.
focusWords.greekHint: Φωνή: ο ήχος που βγάζεις όταν μιλάς ή τραγουδάς.

focusWords.kidDefinition: The air you take into your body and let out.
examples: Before the high note, Mason took a deep breath.
Take a slow breath in, then sing the first line softly.
focusWords.greekHint: Αναπνοή: ο αέρας που παίρνεις και βγάζεις.

focusWords.kidDefinition: To say or sing short words again and again with a rhythm.
examples: The children chanted the name of their team at the match.
We chant the days of the week to a fun beat.
focusWords.greekHint: Τραγουδώ ρυθμικά: λέμε κάτι με ρυθμό, ξανά και ξανά.

focusWords.kidDefinition: A modern style of music that many people enjoy listening to.
examples: Irene loves pop music because the songs are catchy and bright.
Pop music is often played on the radio in the car.
focusWords.greekHint: Μουσική ποπ: σύγχρονο, εύκολο στο άκουσμα στυλ.

focusWords.kidDefinition: Traditional music written by famous composers, often played by orchestras.
examples: Mason's favourite classical music was written by Beethoven.
We listened to classical music while we painted pictures.

focusWords.kidDefinition: A relaxed style of music with a lot of improvisation.
examples: Karen plays the saxophone and loves listening to jazz.
Jazz music sounds smooth and fun on a quiet evening.

lines.text: Hello, friends! I am Lingo, and I love music.
Music is everywhere. You hear it in shops, parks, and even in the kitchen.
Mason likes to hum. Irene carries her flute to school every day.
Today we ask a big question: why do we have music?

question.text: What song makes you want to move, clap, or sing along?

prompt.text: Point to the word for a thing you play to make music.

explain.text: An instrument is something you play to make music.

prompt.text: Listen. Everyone sings the same short words again and again with a beat. Which word is it?

explain.text: When we chant, we say or sing words together with a rhythm.

prompt.text: The singer took a deep ____ before the big note.

explain.text: A breath is the air we take in and let out.

prompt.text: Pop music is a modern style of music that many people enjoy listening to.

explain.text: Pop music is modern and many people enjoy listening to it.

prompt.text: Simon has a beautiful ____! He should be a singer.

explain.text: Your voice is the sound you make when you speak or sing.

prompt.text: Which word is the odd one out? guitar, violin, flute, harp

explain.text: The flute is a wind instrument, but the others are string instruments.

prompt.text: Point to the word for an instrument you hit or shake, like a drum.

explain.text: Percussion instruments make sound when you hit, shake, or tap them.

prompt.text: A flute is a wind instrument, so you play it by blowing air into it.

explain.text: Wind instruments need air blown into them to make sound.

prompt.text: Karen plays the saxophone and loves music that is relaxed and made up as you play. She listens to ____ every night.

explain.text: Jazz is a relaxed style of music with a lot of improvisation.

prompt.text: Point to the word for music written by famous composers like Beethoven.

explain.text: Classical music is written by famous composers and often played by orchestras.

lines.text: Let's play a memory game with our new music words.
Turn the cards over, find the pairs, and say each word out loud.

prompt.text: Tell your partner about the music you love. Use the new words.

frames: I like ___ music because it sounds ___.
Before I sing, I take a deep ___.

model.text: I like pop music because it sounds happy. My favourite instrument is the drum, a percussion instrument. Before I sing, I take a deep breath.

lines.text: Brilliant work, everyone! You now know ten Big Question words.
Music can make us happy, calm, or brave. Keep listening and keep asking why.

exitTicket.text: Name one string instrument, one wind instrument, and one percussion instrument.
Why do you think people sing and chant together?
